---
title: "The course gateway"
subtitle: "What is real in it, what is simulated, and why it exists"
---

The repository ships a gateway that speaks both provider dialects and answers from
rules. Every route points at it by default, which is why the labs, the tests and
the evaluation harness all work with no API key, no network and no GPU.

```bash
make gateway                 # or: docker compose up -d gateway
curl -s localhost:8080/healthz
```

::: {.callout-important}
## Read this before quoting a number it produced

Numbers measured against this gateway are numbers about **this simulator**. They
are correct as measurements of your harness, your guards, your meter and your gates
— the things this course actually teaches — and they are **not evidence about any
model's quality**.

Point a route at a real provider (two environment variables, no code change) and
re-run the same harness when you need that kind of evidence. That substitution
being a config edit is the whole argument of Module 1, and
[ADR 003](https://github.com/MohammadYusif/llm-application-engineering/blob/main/murshid/docs/adr/003-the-course-gateway.md)
records the trade deliberately.
:::

## What is real

| | Why it matters |
|---|---|
| **Both wire contracts** — `POST /v1/chat/completions` and `POST /v1/messages` | your adapters are exercised against the real shapes, including the differences |
| **Token accounting** | `usage`, `prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens`, `cache_read_input_tokens` — the meter measures something real |
| **`finish_reason` control flow** | `length` truncation actually happens when `max_tokens` is too low |
| **Tool calls** | request, `finish_reason=tool_calls`, correlated `tool_result` messages |
| **Structured outputs** | `response_format: json_schema` on one dialect, `output_config.format` on the other |
| **Streaming frames** | SSE deltas, the final usage frame, and Anthropic's typed event stream |
| **Prompt caching** | keyed on a genuinely byte-stable prefix, with a minimum cacheable length (1024 tokens) and a TTL refreshed on hit |
| **HTTP error taxonomy** | 429 with `Retry-After`, 529, 503, 504, and 400 for a missing `max_tokens` |
| **Fault injection** | on a timer, targeted at one model, so the drills are reproducible |
| **Grounding** | answers are composed from the service directory **that arrives in the prompt**. A fact not in the directory cannot appear in an answer |

That last row is the one that makes the golden set meaningful. The don't-know
behaviour is not faked: the simulator matches the citizen's question against the
directory it was given, and when nothing matches it declines — *unless* the prompt
it was served has no don't-know rule, in which case it guesses. Which is exactly
why `answer_faq.v6` fails the gate.

## What is simulated

**Quality.** The model tiers differ by rules, not by capability:

| Tier | Guesses a fee when it should decline | Schema failure, first try | Extra on Arabic | Tool-contract fumble |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `course-flagship` | 0% | 6% | +3% | 2% |
| `course-anthropic` | 0% | 5% | +3% | 2% |
| `course-small` | 34% | 16% | +8% | 14% |
| `murshid-onprem` | 45% | 20% | +14% | 22% |

Those degradations are a **hash of the input**, not a random draw, so a run repeats
exactly and a gate that fires, fires for a reason you can point at.

Latency is simulated too, and compressed by `MOCKGW_SPEED` (default 0.2). Relative
ordering between routes is meaningful; absolute milliseconds are not.

## The drills

```bash
make drill-429       # 429 + Retry-After: 2 on the primary model, three minutes
make drill-outage    # the primary model returns 529 for five minutes
make drill-off
make stats
```

Or directly, with any shape you like:

```bash
curl -s -X POST localhost:8080/admin/fault -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"mode":"rate_limit","seconds":180,"model":"course-flagship","retry_after":2}'
```

| Mode | Response |
|---|---|
| `rate_limit` | 429 with a `Retry-After` header |
| `overload` | 529 |
| `server_error` | 503 |
| `timeout` | hangs, then 504 |
| `off` | end the drill |

`model` targets one model id, which is what makes the fallback drill work: the
primary fails while the on-premise route keeps serving.

## Endpoints

| Endpoint | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `POST /v1/chat/completions` | OpenAI dialect: streaming and not, tools, structured outputs |
| `POST /v1/messages` | Anthropic dialect: top-level `system`, required `max_tokens`, content blocks |
| `GET /v1/models` | model listing |
| `POST /admin/fault` | fault injection |
| `GET /admin/stats` | requests, tokens, cache hits, faults served |
| `POST /admin/reset` | clear stats, faults and the prompt cache |
| `GET /healthz` | liveness |

## Knobs

| Variable | Default | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `MOCKGW_SPEED` | `0.2` | wall-clock compression. `1.0` feels like a real hosted model |
| `MOCKGW_FAST` | unset | `1` disables all sleeping — used by CI |
| `MOCKGW_MIN_CACHEABLE_TOKENS` | `1024` | minimum prefix length before a cache hit is possible |
| `MOCKGW_CACHE_TTL_S` | `300` | prompt-cache TTL, refreshed on hit |

## It has its own tests

A simulator you do not test is a simulator you cannot trust to fail a lab honestly.

```bash
pytest tests/test_gateway_brain.py -q
```

The retrieval table there is the important one: 25 bilingual questions with their
expected directory entry, including four that must match **nothing**. An over-broad
match would turn an out-of-directory question into a confidently wrong answer, and
the groundedness cases would then pass for entirely the wrong reason.
